root_cause: A historic external cron recovery function intentionally grants anonymous EXECUTE alongside a token check. Security advisor recognizes a browser-executable privileged RPC. The repository and inspected current Netlify/scheduled-job sources contain no known client, but an unregistered legacy external caller cannot yet be ruled out.
fix: Prepare a guarded source-controlled ACL migration that preserves the original function and private credential check while allowing only service_role; do not apply until original external consumer and rollback are explicitly attested. Post-cutover negative anonymous tests, positive service_role caller and independent advisor and original cron proof are mandatory.
prevention_rules: Never treat a valid secret token as permission to keep a SECURITY DEFINER RPC callable with anon.
Identify and migrate the original external caller to service_role before revoking anon, preserving the existing recovery executor and cron cadence.
Never apply DDL directly or fake Supabase migration history; use protected source and original provider migration authority.
Require explicit no-anon real ACL readback, original authorized caller smoke test and Supabase advisor zero warning before promoting PROVEN.
A disabled, skipped or failed recovery scheduler cannot be interpreted as a successful security fix.
Open Netlify archive access remains a separate original FAIL that is not affected by this migration.
